methodology_note: Ground truth was constructed in two independent stages to avoid the self-grading problem: (1) candidate shortlisting via mechanical SQL/ILIKE filtering on explicit, literal constraints in each query -- no embeddings, no ranking, no LLM judgment, run by Claude Code against the products table; (2) relevance judged by hand, query by query, applying a consistent 'genuine functional match' standard (e.g. a gel-cream counts as a moisturizer even without the word 'moisturizer' in its name; a face oil, toner, essence, or serum does not count as a moisturizer even if it technically carries the moisturizer category tag; a product bundle/kit/set does not count as a single product match; SPF alone does not disqualify a moisturizer; 'under $X' is strict, 'X or higher' is inclusive). Eight of the twenty queries (1, 7, 9, 14, 16, 18, 19, 20) are excluded from the quantitative Precision/Recall/MRR table because no meaningful, non-arbitrary candidate set could be established for them -- see excluded_queries below for the specific reason per query. This is itself a documented, intentional part of the eval design, not a gap.

7.query_text: sunscreen that doesn't leave a white cast
7.reason: Negation query -- zero literal matches for the phrase 'white cast' anywhere in the catalog's tag-style description field. Not a bug: the catalog's descriptions are short attribute tags, not marketing prose, so a specific negative-attribute phrase like this was never going to appear verbatim. Excluded from quantitative eval; discussed qualitatively as a known hard case for keyword-based negation queries.
